clue.text: Author and diarist with mention of hostilities

indicators.note: a mention is something spoken, so the phrase for the clue's next word is to be said out loud

parts.note: hostilities are fighting, which can be described loosely as 'evil in war'

explanation.surface: A writer who kept a journal recorded the fighting going on around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mention of' asks for the sound: 'evil in war', a loose gloss on 'hostilities', said quickly gives the novelist's name. Treat this as a playful near-homophone, not an exact one.
explanation.definitionFit: The English novelist of Brideshead Revisited also kept diaries that were published after his death.

clue.text: Front position taken by little man having fans?

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession
Ed is a short form of the name Edward, a man's name

explanation.surface: A small man takes the lead and attracts admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fans' looks like admirers; with the question mark it means the blades of a windmill or turbine.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanes are blades turned by wind, like those of a fan, so something fitted with them is described this way.

clue.text: Rooms with boxes containing letters for united nations

indicators.note: the boxes hold the other piece inside them, signalling one piece going inside another

parts.note: loges are boxes in a theatre
UN is the abbreviation for the United Nations

explanation.surface: Theatre boxes are being used to house a UN delegation.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting rooms are the living spaces where people relax, another word for reception rooms.

clue.text: Confection bad for a gut? No!

indicators.note: something bad is spoilt or wrong, so the letters of the words around it are reworked

explanation.surface: A sweet that is not good for the stomach, so refuse it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy sweet made of nuts, honey and sugar is a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: A process for rejecting ham?

parts.note: 'ham' suggests meat, but a ham is an overacting performer, and a trial performance is where poor actors get turned down

explanation.surface: A method of turning away cured pork.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial performance lets a director weed out a poor, overacting performer before casting.

clue.text: Judy's flower arrangement

explanation.surface: Somebody called Judy has arranged some flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Judy is the Hollywood star of The Wizard of Oz, whose surname this is; a wreath of flowers is also called this.

clue.text: One's personal designation? It could be 'anarchist', mine

indicators.note: says these letters might become something else when reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses that the label anarchist might suit them personally.
explanation.definitionFit: A forename given at baptism is the personal part of a person's full name.

clue.text: Woman in the time of king Charles?

definitions.text: in the time of king Charles?

explanation.surface: A lady living under the rule of Charles I or II.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name; also the adjective for the era of the Stuart kings named Charles, from the Latin Carolus.

clue.text: Understand what someone using 'play' on answer phone will do

definitions.text: what someone using 'play' on answer phone will do

explanation.surface: Someone presses play on an answering machine to hear their recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp a point is idiomatically to receive the communication; literally, playing back a recording delivers the recorded words.

clue.text: One who has a belief in British industry

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of the next words, signalled by in

explanation.surface: A person who believes in British manufacturing.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Hinduism is someone holding a religious faith.

clue.text: Think too little of the German with awkward external nature

indicators.note: an external piece goes outside the other, so the jumble wraps around
awkward suggests something ungainly and out of shape, so the word nature is jumbled

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Underestimating a German whose difficult character shows on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' turns NATURE into UNRATE, and 'external' puts that around DER.
explanation.definitionFit: To undervalue someone is to rate them lower than they deserve.

clue.text: At home, poke grandma, having got tense and angry

parts.note: in means at home, as in staying in
dig means a poke, as in a dig in the ribs
nan is an informal British word for a grandmother
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Grandma, poked in her own house, gets wound up and cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Being outraged at unfair treatment is a strong form of feeling cross.

clue.text: Dealing with a fight

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or contest

explanation.surface: A clue about handling a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: A book that concerns a subject is on, or treats of, that topic.

clue.text: Belief can be source of hope in troubled times

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the source of something is where it starts, so take the opening letter of hope

explanation.surface: Faith can bring optimism when life is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'troubled' rearranges H (the 'source of hope') with TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith in a god or gods is a religious conviction.

clue.text: To praise European union record is last thing for some

parts.note: a log is a written record, like a ship's log

indicators.note: the last thing for a word is its final letter, taken from some

explanation.surface: Admiring the European Union is the final item on some people's list.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol someone in speech or writing, especially at a funeral, is to laud them.

clue.text: By the way, you'll find it there!

definitions.text: By the way, you'll find it there!

parts.words: By the way, you'll find it there!
parts.note: 'by the way' looks like an aside, but read literally it means beside the road, which is where the thing is found

explanation.surface: A casual remark telling someone where to look.
explanation.definitionFit: The verge beside a highway is the strip of land along the route.

clue.text: Essential liquid and where it's used in station

parts.note: water is the liquid essential to life
the loo, British slang for a toilet, is where water is used for flushing

explanation.surface: Water and the toilet where it is flushed are both found at a railway station.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British for a toilet; Waterloo is a major London rail terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A major railway terminus in London bears this name, after the battle.

clue.text: Welcome message without the slightest ambiguity

explanation.surface: A greeting that is perfectly clear.
explanation.definitionFit: The signal that danger has passed is a relief to hear; something entirely transparent is perfectly lucid.

clue.text: Poet not much good — just messing about

parts.note: Philip Larkin was an English poet

indicators.note: only a small part of the word good is taken, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A poor-quality poet is only fooling around.
explanation.definitionFit: Larking about is fooling around or playing pranks.

clue.text: French scientist in the morning meeting his father

parts.note: am is the abbreviation for ante meridiem, before noon
pere is French for father, fitting the French scientist

explanation.surface: A French physicist has a morning meeting with his dad.
explanation.definitionFit: Andre-Marie Ampere was a French physicist who pioneered electromagnetism; the unit of current is named after him.

clue.text: Men got a new part for machine

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of the preceding words are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Workers obtained a fresh component for their engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A small generator using permanent magnets, as in an engine's ignition, is a component of machinery.

clue.text: A chance for north, south, east and west to meet

definitions.text: A chance for north, south, east and west to meet

parts.words: A chance for north, south, east and west to meet
parts.note: the compass points look like directions or regions, but they are the four players at a card table

explanation.surface: An opportunity for all parts of the world to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: In the card game the four players sit as North, South, East and West.

clue.text: Troubled reign leads to a republic

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters of reign are shaken up

explanation.surface: A turbulent rule ends in the founding of a republic.
explanation.definitionFit: A West African country, landlocked and named after its great river, is a republic.

clue.text: Shocking eastern chap with admissions of debt

parts.note: Greg is a man's name
IOUs are written notes admitting a debt

explanation.surface: An Eastern man with his debts is outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outstandingly bad is appalling.

clue.text: Drops gong, one landing on street wrong way up

parts.note: an OM, Order of Merit, is a medal or honour, which is gong in British slang
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in a down clue, upside down means the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: A medal is dropped and one lands on the road upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or honour; OM is the Order of Merit. 'wrong way up' reverses ST to TS.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave out something is to drop it from a list.

clue.text: Tim listed out of order and given wrong name

indicators.note: out of order means not in the right sequence, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tim was listed in the wrong place and called by the wrong name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something labelled incorrectly has had an inaccurate heading attached.

clue.text: The late Scot nat Margaret taking English side

parts.note: a wing is a side, of a building or a team

explanation.surface: The late Scottish nationalist Margaret supports England.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Ewing was a Scottish National Party politician; 'Scot nat' is short for Scottish nationalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Ewing was a Scottish National Party MP and MSP who died in 2006.

clue.text: We posed with Hugo, fantastic author

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful and unreal, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We had our pictures taken with Victor Hugo, a superb writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges WE POSED and HUGO; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The English comic novelist created Jeeves and Wooster.
